text: Who has the most MVP awards in MLB history? Bonds, then Ohtani. Barry Bonds has the most MVP awards in MLB history with seven (1990, 1992, 1993 and 2001-2004). Shohei Ohtani is second with four (2021, 2023, 2024 and 2025). Ohtani is a 2026 NL MVP finalist, and the winners will be announced on Thursday, Nov. 12, 2026.. MLB announces the 2026 AL and NL MVP winners on Nov. 12, 2026; Ohtani is a finalist for a fifth MVP.. Eleven players have won exactly three MVP awards, according to MLB.com: Aaron Judge (2022, 2024, 2025), Mike Trout (2014, 2016, 2019), Albert Pujols (2005, 2008, 2009), Alex Rodriguez (2003, 2005, 2007), Mike Schmidt (1980, 1981, 1986), Mickey Mantle (1956, 1957, 1962), Yogi Berra (1951, 1954, 1955), Roy Campanella (1951, 1953, 1955), Stan Musial (1943, 1946, 1948), Joe DiMaggio (1939, 1941, 1947) and Jimmie Foxx (1932, 1933, 1938). Ohtani has won the MVP in each of the past three seasons. He and Frank Robinson are the only players to win MVP in both leagues, and Ohtani is the only one with more than one MVP in each league. The 2026 NL finalists are Ohtani, Pete Crow-Armstrong (Cubs) and Brice Turang (Brewers). The AL finalists are Yordan Alvarez (Astros), Junior Caminero (Rays) and Bobby Witt Jr. (Royals). The MVP is voted on by the Baseball Writers' Association of America, and ballots are cast before the postseason begins.

Has a rookie ever won the Cy Young? Yes, Fernando Valenzuela in 1981. Yes. Fernando Valenzuela of the Los Angeles Dodgers won both the NL Cy Young Award and NL Rookie of the Year in 1981, and he remains the only pitcher in MLB history to win both in the same season. In 2026, Guardians lefty Parker Messick is a finalist for both AL Rookie of the Year and the AL Cy Young.. Parker Messick is a finalist for AL Rookie of the Year (announced Nov. 9, 2026) and the AL Cy Young (Nov. 11, 2026).. Valenzuela went 13-7 with a 2.48 ERA in the strike-shortened 1981 season. He opened the year 8-0 with five shutouts and a 0.50 ERA, setting off "Fernandomania," and the Dodgers went on to win the 1981 World Series. He died in October 2024 at age 63. The 2026 AL Rookie of the Year finalists are Kevin McGonigle (Tigers), Parker Messick (Guardians) and Payton Tolle (Red Sox). The AL Cy Young finalists are Dylan Cease (Blue Jays), Parker Messick (Guardians) and Cam Schlittler (Yankees). Rookie of the Year will be announced on Monday, Nov. 9, 2026, and the Cy Young on Wednesday, Nov. 11. Both awards are voted on by members of the Baseball Writers' Association of America, with ballots submitted before the postseason starts.
